question: Why is "design a notification system" such a common interview question, and what does the low-level core have to cover?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh question isliye favourite hai kyunki ek hi problem do level par poocha ja sakta hai. LLD round mein interviewer classes dekhna chahta hai: notification types, templates, user preferences, channels. HLD round mein woh queues, workers, retries, rate limits aur millions of users ki baat karta hai. Aur asli difficulty follow-ups mein hai -- PLAN.md mein yahi likha hai: "user ne opt out kiya hai", "user ke yahan raat ke 3 baje hain", "push fail hua toh SMS par fallback karo", "client ne request retry ki, user ko OTP do baar nahi jaana chahiye".

Maine stage 1 mein LLD core aise banaya ki in mein se har follow-up ek chhota, local rule ho jiska apna test hai. Core mein yeh cheezein hain: (1) ek catalog of notification TYPES -- category, channels ka order, delivery mode (`all` / `first`) aur har channel ka template; (2) template rendering jahan missing variable error hai; (3) preferences aur quiet hours user ke local time mein; (4) ek hi function `planChannel` jo decide karta hai ki ek channel send hoga, skip hoga ya defer hoga; (5) `Notifier` jo idempotency key, fallback aur `flushDue` sambhalta hai.

Providers sab fake hain -- is project se koi real email, SMS ya push nahi jaata. Stage 1 ke end par 81 tests the aur 43 mutation checks, sab caught. Interview mein main yeh bolunga: sending khud easy hai; engineering un rules mein hai ki KAB, KISKO aur KITNI BAAR bhejna hai.
why_needed: Notification galat jaaye toh seedha user ko dikhta hai: raat 3 baje promo SMS, do baar OTP, ya "Your code is " khaali. Isliye interviewer rules aur edge cases par focus karta hai, sirf "SES call karo" par nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek courier company: parcel bhejna asaan hai, par rules hain -- customer ne "no promotional calls" bola hai, raat ko bell mat bajao, ek address fail ho toh doosra try karo, aur ek hi parcel do baar deliver mat karo.
how_it_works: Request (typeId, userId, data, idempotencyKey) aati hai -> catalog se type -> har channel ka template render -> har channel ke liye planChannel (pending / skipped / deferred) -> record store + key register -> pending deliveries send (all: parallel, first: order mein, first success par ruko) -> deferred wale baad mein flushDue se.
in_this_project: README ka Usage block: `catalog.register({ id: "otp", category: "transactional", mode: "first", channels: ["push", "sms", "email"], templates: {...} })`, phir `new Notifier({ catalog, users, preferences, senders })` aur `notifier.notify({ typeId: "otp", userId: "u1", data: { code: "482913" }, idempotencyKey: "login-7f3a" })`. `npm run demo` (src/demo.ts) OTP fallback, ek retried request aur quiet hours mein deferred marketing dikhata hai. Stage 1 tests: template 9, catalog 17, policy 11, notifier 29, idempotency 7, invariants 8 = 81.

LLD aur HLD dono ke liye ek hi codebase
Fake providers: tests deterministic

Stage 1 mein retries nahi

Idempotency ko 'baad mein dekhenge' bolna

question: What is the difference between a transactional and a marketing notification here, and why does the category decide which preferences apply?
answer_hinglish:
Har notification type ki ek category hoti hai: `transactional` ya `marketing`. Transactional matlab user ne khud kuch kiya aur message usi ka jawab hai -- OTP, password reset, receipt, order shipped. Marketing matlab hum promote kar rahe hain -- sale, weekly digest.

Rule seedha hai aur `planChannel` mein ek jagah likha hai. Transactional mutes aur quiet hours dono ignore karta hai; sirf missing address ek channel skip karta hai. Marketing user ke channel mutes respect karta hai (`skipped (opted_out)`) aur SMS / push quiet hours mein defer hote hain.

Kyun aisa? PLAN.md ka reasoning: agar user sab kuch mute kar sake toh muted OTP user ko account se lock out kar deta hai -- woh login hi nahi kar payega. Aur raat 2 baje user ne khud password reset maanga hai, toh usse subah 7 baje tak rokna bekaar hai. Saath hi transactional messages generally marketing consent rules se exempt hote hain, jabki marketing ke liye user ki choice maanna zaroori hai.

Is design mein category TYPE par hai, request par nahi. Matlab caller har request mein "yeh marketing hai" nahi bolta -- type register karte waqt ek baar decide hota hai, toh koi team galti se promo ko transactional bata kar quiet hours bypass nahi kar sakti jab tak woh catalog mein type hi galat register na kare. Code review ke liye yeh ek jagah hai.
why_needed: Ek hi rule sab par lagao toh ya toh OTP block hoga ya promo raat ko jaayega. Category woh switch hai jo batata hai kaunsi user choice lagu hoti hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank: tumne "no promotional calls" bola hai toh credit card offer ka call nahi aayega, par tumhare card se fraud transaction ka alert phir bhi aayega -- woh tumhari safety ke liye hai.
how_it_works: `planChannel(category, channel, recipient, prefs, now)`: pehle address check (sabke liye), phir `if (category === "transactional") return pending`, uske baad hi mutes aur quiet hours check hote hain.
in_this_project: `src/types.ts` mein `CATEGORIES = ["transactional", "marketing"] as const`. `src/catalog.ts` register mein `isCategory` check karta hai (mutation test case "unknown category"). README ka rules table: transactional "sent anyway" mutes aur quiet hours dono mein. Test `test/notifier.test.ts` "marketing respects mutes; transactional ignores them": user ne sms/push/email sab mute kiye, `sale` suppressed, par `otp` sent. Mutation P1 (transactional respects mutes) aur P3 (mutes ignored) dono pakde gaye.

Rule ek function mein

question: What are the two delivery modes "all" and "first", and when would you choose each?
answer_hinglish:
Type ka `mode` batata hai ki uske channels ke saath kya karna hai. `all`: har allowed channel par bhejo, parallel mein, aur ek channel fail hone se baaki nahi rukte -- jaise order shipped ka push AUR email dono. `first`: channels ko order mein try karo, jo pehla succeed kare woh jeet gaya, aur jo channels abhi wait kar rahe the woh `skipped (not_needed)` ban jaate hain -- jaise OTP: push, warna SMS, warna email.

PLAN.md ne do modes recommend kiye, ek mode with flags nahi, kyunki real products ko yahi do shapes chahiye. OTP ko teen jagah bhejna galat hai (user confuse hota hai, aur SMS ka paisa lagta hai), aur order update ko sirf ek jagah bhejna bhi galat hai.

`first` mode mein kya "fail" maana jaata hai? Permanent failure, retryable failure, aur sender jo throw kare -- teeno next channel par fall through karte hain, kyunki stage 1 mein retries nahi hain. Ek interesting case: marketing `first` type quiet hours mein -- push aur SMS deferred hain, email deferred nahi hota, toh email abhi deliver ho jaata hai aur deferred channels `not_needed` ho jaate hain. Rule hai "jo pehla channel ABHI deliver kar sake woh jeetega".

`all` sach mein parallel hai: test "a slow push does not hold the email back" yeh prove karta hai, aur mutation N10 (all sequential) pakdi gayi.
why_needed: Kuch messages ko user tak kisi bhi ek raste se pahunchna hai (OTP), kuch ko har raste se (receipt). Ek hi behaviour dono ke liye galat hoga.
real_world_analogy: `first`: dost ko pehle call karo, na uthaye toh WhatsApp, phir bhi nahi toh email -- jaise hi baat ho gayi, ruk jao. `all`: shaadi ka card -- WhatsApp bhi, post bhi, dono bhejo.
how_it_works: `Notifier.run`: `all` mein `Promise.all(chosen.map(attempt))`; `first` mein `for` loop, `if (await this.attempt(...)) { markRestNotNeeded(record); return; }`. `markRestNotNeeded` har pending ya deferred delivery ko skipped not_needed karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::run` aur `src/record.ts::markRestNotNeeded`. Tests in `test/notifier.test.ts`: '"first" stops at the first success: later channels are not_needed and never called', '"first" falls through failures, permanent or retryable, and a throwing sender', '"all": one channel failing does not stop the others', '"first" marketing in quiet hours: email (not deferred) delivers now'. Mutation N3 (`first` keeps going after a success) caught.

all mode mein slow channel baaki ko nahi rokta
disadvantages: first mode sequential hai: har fail channel latency add karta hai
Stage 1 mein retry nahi, ek retryable fail bhi seedha next channel
common_mistakes: first mode mein success ke baad bhi baaki channels bhejna

question: Why is a notification type data in a catalog rather than a class, and what does the catalog check at registration?
answer_hinglish:
Ek type (`order_shipped`, `otp`, `weekly_digest`) ka behaviour alag nahi hota -- sirf uska DATA alag hota hai: category, channels ka order, mode aur har channel ka template. Isliye `NotificationTypeDef` ek plain object hai aur `NotificationCatalog` ek Map. Class per type banate toh 50 types ke 50 classes hote jinme sirf strings alag hain; naya type add karne ke liye deploy chahiye hota. Data ho toh kal yeh config ya DB se bhi load ho sakta hai.

Sabse important decision: sab kuch REGISTRATION par check hota hai, yaani startup par, na ki jab pehla user type trigger kare. `register()` yeh check karta hai: id format (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$/`), duplicate id (`DUPLICATE_TYPE`), known category, mode `all` ya `first`, kam se kam ek channel, har channel known aur repeat nahi, har listed channel ka exactly ek template (unlisted channel ka template bhi error), non-empty body, email ke liye subject zaroori, SMS / push par subject mana, aur koi malformed `{{` nahi. Sab `INVALID_TYPE` hain.

Phir catalog caller ke object ka COPY store karta hai. Agar original object store hota, toh caller baad mein `def.channels.push("sms")` karke registered type badal sakta tha -- bina kisi validation ke. Mutation C1 (caller's object stored) isi test se pakdi gayi.

Interview point: "fail fast at startup" -- template typo production mein raat 2 baje nahi, deploy ke waqt pakda jaata hai.
why_needed: Template ka typo ya missing email subject runtime par user ke saamne fail ho toh bahut late hai. Registration par check karne se galti deploy time par dikhti hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant ka menu card print hone se pehle proofread hota hai -- galat price customer ke order karne par nahi, printing se pehle pakdi jaati hai. Aur menu ki copy kitchen mein lagti hai, taaki koi waiter apni copy par pen se badal de toh kitchen par asar na ho.
how_it_works: `register(def)` checks ki ek line chalata hai; koi bhi fail ho toh throw aur Map mein kuch nahi jaata. Pass ho toh `channels: [...def.channels]` aur har template ka `{ ...templates[c] }` copy store hota hai.
in_this_project: `src/catalog.ts::NotificationCatalog.register`. `test/catalog.test.ts` (17 tests): '14 kinds of invalid type' ek `it.each` table hai ("bad id", "channel twice", "template for an unlisted channel", "email without subject", "subject on push", "malformed placeholder in subject" ...), har ek `INVALID_TYPE` aur `c.ids()` empty. Mutation C2 (duplicate channel accepted) pehli run mein survive hui thi -- test ka type kisi aur wajah se bhi invalid tha; test fix hua. Stage 3 mein `in_app` aaya: uska subject allowed hai (item ka title).

question: How does template rendering work, and why is a missing value an error instead of an empty string?
answer_hinglish:
Template mein placeholders `{{name}}` ya dotted `{{user.name}}` hote hain; braces ke andar spaces allowed hain (`{{ user.name }}`). Ek regex `PLACEHOLDER` har match ko replace karta hai, aur `lookup(data, path)` path ko `.` se todkar data mein ek ek step neeche jaata hai.

Missing value -- property hai hi nahi, `null` hai ya `undefined` hai -- `TEMPLATE_VARIABLE_MISSING` error hai. PLAN.md ka reasoning: "Your OTP is " khaali ke saath user ko bhejna kuch na bhejne se bura hai. User confuse hota hai, support ticket banta hai, aur bug chupa rehta hai. Error hone par caller ko turant pata chalta hai, aur kyunki rendering `notify()` ke synchronous half mein hota hai, kuch store nahi hota.

Value types bhi strict hain: string, finite number, boolean chalega. Object ya array `[object Object]` render karta, isliye refuse; `NaN` aur `Infinity` bhi refuse (`INVALID_REQUEST`). Numbers aur booleans `String()` se -- `0` aur `false` valid values hain, missing nahi.

Teen subtle cheezein: (1) sirf OWN properties padhi jaati hain (`Object.hasOwn`), toh `{{constructor}}` missing hai, `function Object()` nahi. (2) Replace callback function hai, toh value mein `$&` ya `$1` literal rehta hai -- string replacement pattern ki tarah interpret nahi hota. (3) Value dobara render nahi hoti: value `"{{b}}"` literal `{{b}}` hi rahegi. Aur important: `buildRecord` type ke HAR channel ko render karta hai, chahe user woh channel skip kare.
why_needed: Template aur data alag teams ke paas hote hain. Mismatch silently khaali string ban jaaye toh bug production mein users ko dikhta hai; error se woh caller ko dikhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Form letter: "Dear ____, aapka parcel ____ ship hua." Agar naam blank reh gaya toh letter post karne se pehle clerk ko wapas do -- blank letter bhejna sharmindagi hai.
how_it_works: `renderText(text, data, escape)` = `text.replace(PLACEHOLDER, (_m, path) => { const v = lookup(data, path); return escape ? escapeHtml(v) : v; })`. `lookup` har part par `current === null || typeof current !== "object" || !Object.hasOwn(current, part)` check karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/template.ts`: `PLACEHOLDER`, `lookup`, `renderText`, `renderTemplate`. `test/template.test.ts` (9 tests): "a missing, null or undefined value is an error, never an empty string" (`{{a.b}}` with `a: "text"` bhi missing), "renders numbers and booleans, refuses objects, arrays, NaN and Infinity" (`{ n: 20, b: false, z: 0 }` -> "20 false 0"), "a value that looks like a placeholder is not rendered again, and $ patterns are literal". Mutations T3 (undefined rendered) aur T7 (NaN / Infinity rendered) caught.

Errors machine-readable code ke saath
0 aur false sahi render hote hain
disadvantages: Koi default value syntax nahi (`{{name|there}}` jaisa)
Koi loops / conditionals nahi -- jaan boojh kar simple

question: Why are values HTML-escaped only in email bodies, and what goes wrong if you escape everywhere or nowhere?
answer_hinglish:
Escaping ka rule context par depend karta hai, isliye project mein yeh ek flag hai, global setting nahi. Email body HTML hai: agar user ka naam `` ya `` hai aur hum use as-is daal dein, toh email client mein HTML injection ho sakta hai (phishing link, broken layout). Isliye email body ki VALUES `escapeHtml` se jaati hain -- template text khud escape nahi hota, kyunki woh humne likha hai aur usme intentional `

` hai. SMS aur push plain text hain. Wahan escape karoge toh user ko `Tom & Jerry` dikhega -- yeh bug hai, safety nahi. Email ka SUBJECT bhi plain text hai (mail client use text ki tarah dikhata hai), isliye `renderTemplate` subject ko `escape: false` se render karta hai aur sirf body ko `html` flag milta hai. Mutation T5 (subject escaped) yahi check karti hai. `in_app` bhi escape nahi hota -- app text render karta hai. `escapeHtml` mein order bhi matter karta hai: `&` sabse pehle replace hota hai. Agar `<` pehle `<` banta aur phir `&` replace hota, toh `<` `<` ban jaata -- double escaping. Test "escapeHtml escapes & first" (`"<&>"` -> `"<&>"`) aur mutation T6 yeh lock karte hain. Paanch characters escape hote hain: `& < > " '`. Interview line: "escape at output, for the output's context" -- input par ek baar escape karke store karna galat hai, kyunki ek hi data teen contexts mein jaata hai.
why_needed: Ek hi data HTML email, plain SMS aur push teeno mein jaata hai. Har context ka escaping alag hai; galat jagah escape karna ya na karna dono bugs hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi address teen jagah likhna: courier ke form mein (format strict), WhatsApp par (seedha text) aur ek printed letter par. Har jagah ke apne rules hain -- form wala format WhatsApp par lagao toh ajeeb lagega.
how_it_works: `buildRecord` har channel ke liye `renderTemplate(template, data, channel === "email")` bulata hai. `renderTemplate` body ko `html` flag se aur subject ko hamesha `false` se render karta hai.
in_this_project:
`src/template.ts::escapeHtml` aur `renderTemplate`; `src/planner.ts::buildRecord` mein `channel === "email"`. Tests: "HTML-escapes values only when asked (email bodies), never the template text itself" (` & 'co'` -> `<script>alert("x")...`), "an email subject is plain text; only the body is escaped" (`{ subject: "Hi A&B", body: "

A&B

" }`). Notifier test '"all" sends every channel ... email body escaped, push not'. Mutations T1, T5, T6 caught.

Template text trusted, sirf values escape
Order bug test se locked
disadvantages: Sirf HTML body context; URL attribute ke andar value (href) ka alag escaping nahi hai
Real email clients ke quirks test nahi hue (fake providers)

question: What could a caller do through the request data or a template if rendering were naive, and how does this code close each hole?
answer_hinglish:
Data caller se aata hai (stage 3 mein seedha HTTP body se), toh usse untrusted maanna chahiye. Naive renderer mein chaar holes hote hain, aur code har ek ko alag se band karta hai.

Pehla: prototype reach. Naive `data[part]` lookup `{{constructor}}` par `function Object() { [native code] }` aur `{{a.toString}}` par function ka source render kar deta -- internals leak aur ajeeb output. Yahan `Object.hasOwn` hai, toh sirf data ki apni properties padhi jaati hain; yeh missing variable error ban jaata hai. Mutation T2 (inherited properties readable) caught.

Doosra: re-rendering. Agar output ko dobara render karte, toh user ka naam `{{otherField}}` rakh kar woh doosri fields nikalwa sakta tha (template injection). Yahan ek hi `replace` pass hai; value `"{{b}}"` literal rehti hai.

Teesra: replacement patterns. `String.replace` ko string doge toh `$&`, `$1` special hain -- value `$&` poora match insert kar degi. Callback function dene se value as-is jaati hai.

Chautha: data shape. `checkRequest` sirf plain object maanta hai (prototype `Object.prototype` ya `null`) -- `new Date()` ya array `INVALID_REQUEST` hai. Values string / finite number / boolean hi chalengi.

Template side par: malformed braces (`{{order-id}}`, `{{a}`) registration par `INVALID_TYPE` -- warna woh literal user ko chale jaate. Templates developers likhte hain aur catalog mein register hote hain; is project mein users templates nahi likhte, toh template ko trusted maana hai -- yeh assumption bolna zaroori hai.
why_needed: Notification API ek service ke liye open hai; uska data kisi bhi form mein aa sakta hai. Renderer ko yeh maan kar likhna padta hai ki data hostile ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek photocopy shop jo form bharta hai: woh sirf tumhare diye hue kaagaz se naam leta hai, apni dukaan ke register se nahi; aur agar tumne naam ki jagah "jo bhi register mein likha ho" likha, toh woh literally wahi likh dega, register nahi kholega.
how_it_works: Ek regex pass, callback replacement, `Object.hasOwn` lookup, strict value types; `checkRequest` mein `isPlainObject`; `placeholders()` mein regex hata kar bache text mein `{{` ya `}}` mila toh error.
in_this_project: `src/template.ts` (`lookup`, `renderText`, `placeholders`), `src/planner.ts::checkRequest` aur `isPlainObject`. Tests: "reads only own properties: {{constructor}} and {{toString}} are missing", "a value that looks like a placeholder is not rendered again, and $ patterns are literal" (`{ a: "$& $1 $$" }` -> same string), "placeholders() ... rejects malformed braces" (`{{ bad-name }}`, `{{a}`, `a}}`, `{{}}`, `{{1x}}`). Notifier test "data a class instance" -> `INVALID_REQUEST`. Mutations T2, T4, N13 caught.
advantages: Har hole ka apna test aur mutation
Logic-less template: attack surface chhota
Data shape strict
disadvantages: Templates trusted maane gaye hain; user-authored templates ke liye sandbox nahi
Data size limit library mein nahi (HTTP layer 64 KB lagata hai)
common_mistakes: `data[part]` bina own-property check
Output ko dobara template engine mein daalna
Full-featured engine (code execution) user input ke saath

question: How are user preferences modelled (marketing mutes and quiet hours), and which one wins when both apply?
answer_hinglish:
Preferences do cheezein hain: `mutedMarketing` -- channels ki list jo user ne marketing ke liye band ki (default khaali, yaani sab allowed), aur optional `quietHours: { start, end }` -- `HH:MM` format mein user ke local time mein. Dono sirf marketing par lagte hain; transactional ko yeh dikhte hi nahi.

Jab dono apply hon -- user ne push mute kiya hai aur abhi uske quiet hours bhi hain -- toh MUTE jeetta hai: delivery `skipped (opted_out)` hoti hai, `deferred` nahi. Logic simple hai: deferred ka matlab "baad mein bhejenge", par user ne kaha hai "kabhi mat bhejo". Deferred rakhte toh subah woh mute ke bawajood chala jaata. `planChannel` mein mute check quiet-hours check se PEHLE hai, aur test "a muted channel is skipped even in quiet hours (opted out wins over deferred)" yeh lock karta hai.

`PreferenceStore.set` validate karta hai: time `HH:MM` hi (`24:00` ya `7:00` reject), start aur end barabar nahi (khaali window ya poora din? ambiguous, isliye reject), aur mute list mein sirf known channels. Galat input par purani preferences waise hi rehti hain. `get` copy return karta hai, taaki caller returned object badal kar stored preferences na badal sake. Jo user kabhi set hi nahi kiya, uske liye `{ mutedMarketing: [] }` default.

Stage 3 mein yeh shape HTTP se aane laga, tab ek gap mila: `{"quietHours": null}` par TypeError aata tha -- ab shape check hota hai aur `INVALID_PREFERENCES` milta hai.
why_needed: User ko control chahiye ki promo kahan aur kab aaye. Do simple controls (channel mute, quiet window) zyada tar products ke liye kaafi hain.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ke bahar "No hawkers" board (mute) aur "2 se 4 baje bell mat bajao" (quiet hours). Agar "No hawkers" laga hai toh hawker 4 baje ke baad bhi nahi aayega -- board ki baat pehle aati hai.
how_it_works: `planChannel`: no address -> transactional -> `prefs.mutedMarketing.includes(channel)` -> quiet hours (`WAKES_USER` channels only) -> pending. Order hi precedence hai.
in_this_project: `src/preferences.ts::PreferenceStore` (`set` validation, `get` copies, `parseHhMm`), `src/policy.ts::planChannel`. `test/policy.test.ts`: "rejects bad times, equal start/end, unknown channels; keeps the old value", "returns copies", "a muted channel is skipped even in quiet hours", aur stage 3 ka "not an object, or quietHours not an object -> INVALID_PREFERENCES, not a TypeError". Mutation Q7 (start = end accepted) caught.

question: Walk through quietUntil: how does it work out local time, a window that crosses midnight, the exclusive end, and times before 1970?
answer_hinglish:
`quietUntil(now, utcOffsetMinutes, quiet)` ek hi sawaal ka jawab deta hai: agar `now` user ke quiet hours ke andar hai, toh woh epoch ms jab quiet hours khatam honge; warna `undefined`.

Step 1: local time. `local = now + offset * MINUTE_MS`. UTC+5:30 ke liye offset 330 hai, toh 17:00 UTC local 22:30 ban jaata hai.

Step 2: din ke andar kitna time hua. `intoDay = ((local % DAY_MS) + DAY_MS) % DAY_MS`. Yeh double modulo zaroori hai: JavaScript mein `%` negative number par negative result deta hai, toh 1970 se pehle ke time par plain `%` negative "time of day" deta. Mutation Q5 isi ki thi, aur pehli run mein SURVIVE hui -- test 23:00 use karta tha jahan galat arithmetic bhi sahi jawab de deti hai. Noon ka case add kiya, tab pakdi gayi.

Step 3: do window shapes. `start < end` (jaise 12:00-13:30): quiet agar `start <= intoDay < end`. Warna window midnight cross karti hai (22:00-07:00): agar `intoDay >= start` toh khatam KAL ke `end` par (`dayStart + DAY_MS + end`), agar `intoDay < end` toh AAJ ke `end` par, warna quiet nahi. Start inclusive, end exclusive -- 07:00 par quiet khatam.

Step 4: wapas UTC: `endLocal - offset * MINUTE_MS`.

Har boundary dono taraf tested hai: 21:59 nahi, 22:00 haan, 06:59 haan, 07:00 nahi. Mutations Q1-Q8 (end inclusive, start exclusive, midnight-crossing end galat din par, offset sign, negative modulo, ...) sab caught.
why_needed: Quiet hours ka poora faayda isi function ki correctness par hai. Off-by-one ya galat din ka matlab hai raat ko promo ya subah ka message dopahar ko.
real_world_analogy: Raat ki shift 22:00 se 07:00: agar tum 23:00 par pahunche toh shift kal subah 07:00 khatam hogi; agar 02:00 par pahunche toh AAJ subah 07:00. Ghadi dekhkar decide karna hota hai ki "kaunsa 07:00".
how_it_works: Pure function: koi state nahi, sirf arithmetic. `parseHhMm` minutes deta hai, `MINUTE_MS` aur `DAY_MS` constants. Offset user directory mein validate hota hai (-720 se 840 minutes, integer).
in_this_project: `src/preferences.ts::quietUntil`, `validateOffset`. `test/policy.test.ts`: "window crossing midnight: start inclusive, end exclusive" (`at(22,0)` -> `at(31)` yaani agle din 07:00), "window inside one day", "uses the user's local time: 17:00 UTC is 22:30 at UTC+5:30, quiet until 07:00 local = 01:30 UTC", negative offset (03:00 UTC at UTC-5 -> 12:00 UTC), "works for times before 1970". Randomized test isse independently `Date` ke `getUTCHours` se re-compute karta hai.
advantages: Pure function, ManualClock ke bina bhi test hoti hai
Dono window shapes ek jagah
Boundaries dono taraf tested
disadvantages: Fixed offset: DST nahi
Har call par `parseHhMm` dobara (sasta, par cache nahi)
common_mistakes: Plain % with negative epoch
Midnight-crossing window ka end hamesha 'kal' maan lena
Offset ka sign ulta (local = now - offset)
End inclusive
follow_up_questions: Why does the test use noon before 1970 and not 23:00?
How would DST change this function?
Why is the end exclusive?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fixed offset se function pure aur sasta hai -- koi tz database nahi. Keemat: DST zones mein saal ke aadhe hisse ek ghanta off. Epoch ms + offset arithmetic ek simple model hai jo interview mein samjhaana easy hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat offset (sign ulta) se poore region ko din mein bhi quiet maana jaayega ya raat ko bhi nahi. Isiliye Q4 mutation aur negative offset test hai. Window ka sirf 15 minute ka gap ho (00:15-00:00) toh deferred message ke liye flush us gap mein chalna chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: IANA zone (`Asia/Kolkata`) store karke `Intl.DateTimeFormat` ya Temporal / luxon se local wall-clock nikaalna; ya window ko UTC intervals mein pre-compute karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Function per-delivery O(1) hai, scale problem nahi. 100x par cost tz library ki ho jaayegi agar IANA zones lo -- formatter ko zone ke hisaab se cache karna padega.
advanced.production_improvements: IANA zone, DST transition ke din ke tests (spring forward mein 02:30 exist nahi karta), weekday / weekend windows, aur user ka zone device se auto-update.

question: Why do quiet hours defer a message instead of dropping it, and why is email never deferred?
answer_hinglish:
Quiet hours ka maqsad user ko neend mein disturb na karna hai, message ko maarna nahi. Marketing message jo 23:00 par trigger hua, woh subah 07:00 par bhi relevant ho sakta hai, toh SMS aur push ko `deferred` mark karke `notBefore` = window ka end set hota hai; `flushDue()` baad mein bhejta hai. Drop karte toh har raat wale campaign ka ek hissa silently gaayab ho jaata, aur caller ko pata bhi nahi chalta.

Email kyun nahi? Email kisi ko jagata nahi -- phone buzz nahi karta (zyada tar setups mein), user inbox subah dekhta hai. Isliye `WAKES_USER = new Set(["sms", "push"])` hai, aur sirf in channels par quiet hours lagte hain. Stage 3 ka `in_app` bhi kisi ko nahi jagata, woh bhi defer nahi hota. Mutation P2 (email deferred too) pakdi gayi.

Iska ek nice side effect `first` mode mein dikhta hai: marketing `promo_first` (push, sms, email) raat ko trigger hua -- push aur sms deferred, email pending. "Jo pehla channel ABHI deliver kar sake" rule se email abhi jaata hai aur deferred channels `not_needed` ho jaate hain. Agar email fail ho jaaye, deferred channels wait karte hain aur subah flush par first success par ruk jaate hain.

Trade-off honestly: deferral ka matlab state rakhna (record memory mein) aur ek poller (`flushDue`). Stale message ka risk bhi hai -- "sale khatam hone mein 1 ghanta" subah tak bekaar. Is project mein expiry / TTL per type nahi hai; production mein `expiresAt` hona chahiye.
why_needed: User ki raat bhi bachani hai aur business ka message bhi. Defer dono ko balance karta hai; drop ek ko poori tarah haar deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Raat ko aaya courier guard ke paas rakh diya jaata hai aur subah ghar pahunchta hai -- waapas nahi bheja jaata. Par letter box mein chitthi daalna (email) raat ko bhi theek hai, kisi ko jagata nahi.
how_it_works: `planChannel`: marketing + `prefs.quietHours` + `WAKES_USER.has(channel)` -> `quietUntil(...)`; agar defined toh `{ status: "deferred", to, notBefore: until }`. `flushDue` jab `notBefore <= now` ho tab delivery ko dobara plan karke bhejta hai.
in_this_project: `src/policy.ts::WAKES_USER`. `test/notifier.test.ts` "quiet hours defer marketing sms/push, flushDue sends them when due, not before": 23:00 par `push:deferred sms:deferred email:sent`, status `scheduled`, `notBefore` = agle din 07:00; 06:59:59.999 par flush 0 bhejta hai, 07:00 par 2. '"first" marketing in quiet hours: email (not deferred) delivers now, the deferred channels become not_needed'. Mutation N15 (due at notBefore exclusive) aur N18 (deferred not marked not_needed) caught.

Email turant deliver: first mode mein raat ko bhi user tak pahunchta hai
Ek set mein likha rule: kaun jagata hai
disadvantages: Deferred state memory mein (stage 1 restart par lost)
Message ki expiry nahi: stale promo subah bhi jaata hai
Subah 07:00 par saare deferred ek saath (thundering herd)

Email ko bhi defer karna
Deferred ko transactional par bhi lagana

question: Quiet hours use a fixed UTC offset per user with no DST. What breaks in production, and how would you do it properly?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: is project mein user ka `utcOffsetMinutes` fixed hai (-720 se 840, integer), aur DST handle nahi hota. README ke "Known and NOT handled" mein yeh clearly likha hai, chhupaya nahi.

Kya toot-ta hai: New York ka user winter mein UTC-5 aur summer mein UTC-4 hai. Agar offset -300 store hai, toh summer mein uske 22:00-07:00 quiet hours asal mein 23:00-08:00 local par lagenge -- raat 22:30 par promo push aa sakta hai, aur subah 07:30 tak ruka rahega. Saal ke aadhe hisse ek ghanta off. India (UTC+5:30, no DST) jaise users ke liye koi problem nahi, isliye bug region-specific dikhta hai -- yeh support tickets mein "kuch users ko raat ko message aata hai" ki tarah aata hai, reproduce karna mushkil.

Sahi tareeka: user ka IANA zone store karo (`America/New_York`), offset nahi. Har check par `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (ya Temporal / luxon) se `now` ka local wall-clock time nikaalo, aur window ka end bhi zone ke hisaab se compute karo -- kyunki DST transition wale din "07:00 kal" 23 ya 25 ghante door ho sakta hai, aur spring-forward par 02:30 exist hi nahi karta. Zone device / app se aata hai aur travel par update hota hai.

Is project ka design isse kitna aasan banata hai: time ka saara arithmetic `quietUntil` mein hai aur rule `planChannel` mein, aur `flushDue` send time par REPLAN karta hai. Toh zone support ek function badalna aur tests add karna hai, poora notifier nahi.
why_needed: Global product mein users DST zones mein hain. Galat local time ka matlab hai quiet hours ka promise toota, jo trust aur kuch jagah regulation dono ka issue hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek purani ghadi jo daylight saving par aage nahi badhti: saal ke aadhe hisse tumhara alarm ek ghanta galat bajta hai, aur sirf un shehron mein jahan DST hai.
how_it_works: Abhi: `local = now + offset`. Properly: `local wall-clock = tz(now, zone)`, window end = next occurrence of `end` in that zone converted back to an instant.
in_this_project: `src/types.ts` mein `utcOffsetMinutes?: number; // ... (fixed; DST not handled). Default 0.` `src/preferences.ts::validateOffset` range check karta hai, `src/users.ts` upsert par bulata hai. Randomized test offsets `[-300, 0, 60, 330, 345, 600]` use karta hai -- sab fixed. DST ka koi test nahi, kyunki feature nahi hai.

Change ek function tak simit
Limitation documented
disadvantages: DST zones mein saal ke aadhe hisse 1 ghanta galat
User travel kare toh offset purana
common_mistakes: Server ke local time zone mein quiet hours nikaalna
Offset ko zone samajhna
DST transition day test na karna
follow_up_questions: How do you compute the end of a window on the day clocks spring forward?
Where does the user's zone come from, and how often does it change?
Would you pre-compute quiet windows as UTC intervals?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Offset vs zone: offset ek integer, pure arithmetic, koi data dependency nahi. Zone sahi hai par tz database (jo badalta rehta hai, countries DST rules badalte hain) par dependent hai aur har check thoda mehenga.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Zone galat ya missing ho toh fallback chahiye (UTC ya last known). Tz database purana ho toh naye rules wale desh galat. Spring-forward par jo window end exist nahi karta, uske liye next valid instant lena padta hai.
advanced.alternatives: (1) IANA zone + Intl / Temporal. (2) Quiet window ko har user ke liye agle 48 h ke UTC intervals mein pre-compute karke store karna. (3) Device local time par client-side decision (push ke liye OS-level "Do Not Disturb" bhi hota hai).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Lakhon users par har delivery ke liye formatter banana mehenga -- zone ke hisaab se `Intl.DateTimeFormat` cache karo. Deferred deliveries ko zone ke hisaab se bucket karke 07:00 local par spread karna padega.

question: Why is the whole send / skip / defer decision a single function, planChannel, and who calls it?
answer_hinglish:
README ka rules table -- no address, mute, quiet hours, email exception, transactional bypass -- poora ka poora ek function hai: `planChannel(category, channel, recipient, prefs, now)` in `src/policy.ts`. Yeh pure hai: input lo, `ChannelPlan` return karo (`pending` with `to`, `deferred` with `notBefore`, ya `skipped` with reason). Koi I/O nahi, koi state nahi, time bhi parameter hai.

Kyun ek jagah? Pehla, review: product manager poochhe "marketing SMS raat ko jaata hai?", toh jawab 15 lines mein hai, 5 files mein bikhra nahi. Doosra, consistency: yeh rule do jagah chahiye -- jab request aati hai (`buildRecord`) aur jab deferred delivery due hoti hai (`replan`). Agar logic duplicate hota toh dono versions alag ho jaate. Late-flush bug ka fix exactly yahi tha: send time par SAME function dobara chalao. Stage 2 ka `QueuedNotifier` bhi jab job run hota hai tab isi ko call karta hai. Teesra, testing: pure function ko bina notifier ke test kar sakte ho -- `test/policy.test.ts` ka "planChannel: the one rule" block.

Order bhi decision hai: address check sabse pehle (transactional ke liye bhi -- address nahi toh bhej hi nahi sakte), phir transactional bypass, phir mute, phir quiet hours. Isse "mute wins over deferred" aur "transactional ignores everything except no address" automatically milta hai.

Stage 3 mein `in_app` aaya toh is function ko chhuna hi nahi pada: `addressFor` user id deta hai aur `in_app` `WAKES_USER` mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Business rules jab code mein bikhar jaate hain toh do jagah alag behave karte hain. Ek pure function ek source of truth hai jise notify time aur send time dono use karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek office ka single rulebook jo reception aur security guard dono padhte hain. Agar dono ke paas apni apni notes hon toh ek din reception andar bhej dega aur guard rok dega.
how_it_works: `buildRecord` har channel ke liye `applyPlan(delivery, planChannel(...))`. `replan(deps, record, delivery, now)` user aur preferences FRESH lekar `planChannel` dobara bulata hai; user hi delete ho gaya toh `skipped no_address`.
in_this_project: `src/policy.ts::planChannel` (file ke top par rule comment ke roop mein bhi likha hai). Callers: `src/planner.ts::buildRecord`, `src/planner.ts::replan` (stage 1 `flushDue` aur stage 2 job dono). Tests: "no address skips the channel for every category; a blank address counts as none", "transactional ignores mutes and quiet hours", "marketing: muted channel skipped ..., sms/push deferred at night, email never deferred". Mutations P1-P4 caught.

question: Walk through Notifier.notify(): what happens in the synchronous half and why does "check everything, then change state" matter?
answer_hinglish:
`notify()` ke do halves hain, aur file ke top comment mein yahi likha hai.

Synchronous half (`accept`): (1) `checkRequest` -- key non-empty string, max 255 chars, data plain object; yahi request ka fingerprint banata hai. (2) Key pehle se hai? Fingerprint same toh wahi entry return (duplicate), alag toh `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. (3) `buildRecord` -- type lookup (`UNKNOWN_TYPE`), user lookup (`UNKNOWN_USER`), preferences, aur type ke HAR channel ke liye: sender hai? (`NO_SENDER`), template render (missing variable throw karta hai), `planChannel`. Yeh record abhi kahin store nahi hai. (4) Code comment: "Nothing above changed any state. From here on, nothing throws." -- record store, key register, aur `run()` shuru.

Asynchronous half: `run` pending deliveries bhejta hai, aur `notify` `entry.done` await karke record ka copy return karta hai.

"Check everything, then change state" (projects/17-parking-lot wala pattern) ka matlab: jo bhi throw ho sakta hai woh state badalne se PEHLE hota hai. Isliye error = "kuch nahi hua": koi record nahi, koi send nahi, aur idempotency key free hai -- caller data theek karke SAME key se retry kar sakta hai. Agar beech mein store karke phir template fail hota, toh ek aadha record padha rehta aur key "used" ho jaati; retry `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` ya galat record deta.

Ek detail: `notify` `async` hai, toh `accept` ka throw rejected promise ban jaata hai -- caller `await` karke catch karta hai. Aur `get()` `structuredClone` return karta hai, live record nahi (mutation N14).
why_needed: Partial state sabse bure bugs deta hai: aadha record, used key, koi send nahi. Pehle validate, phir commit -- error ka matlab hamesha "nothing happened".
real_world_analogy: Bank form: clerk pehle saare fields check karta hai, signature, KYC -- tab jaakar account mein entry karta hai. Aadhe mein galti mili toh form wapas, ledger mein kuch nahi likha.
how_it_works: `accept(request)`: `checkRequest` -> `keys.get(key)` -> `buildRecord` (pure, throws) -> `records.set` -> `keys.set` -> `entry.done = this.run(...)`. Sab synchronous, koi `await` nahi.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::accept`, `src/planner.ts::checkRequest`, `src/planner.ts::buildRecord`. Test block "errors mean nothing happened" in `test/notifier.test.ts`: `it.each` unknown type, unknown user, missing variable, data array, data `new Date()`, empty key, key of 256 chars -- har case mein `notifier.list()` empty, zero provider attempts, aur valid key ke saath dobara bhejo toh `delivered`. Mutations N6 (missing sender not checked), N12 (blank key accepted), N13 (non-plain data accepted), N19 (key not registered) caught.
advantages: Error ka matlab hamesha 'nothing happened'
Key free rehti hai, safe retry
Ek synchronous block: concurrency bhi safe
disadvantages: Har channel render hota hai chahe skip ho (thoda extra kaam)
Sab validation upfront: lamba synchronous block
common_mistakes: Pehle record save, phir validate
Key ko validation se pehle register karna
Live record return karna

question: How do 20 concurrent identical notify() calls end up as one record and one send, without any lock?
answer_hinglish:
Trick yeh hai ki idempotency key `notify()` ke SYNCHRONOUS part mein register hoti hai, pehle `await` se pehle. JavaScript single-threaded event loop hai: ek synchronous block poora chalta hai, beech mein koi doosra callback nahi aa sakta. Toh pehli call `accept()` mein key check karti hai (nahi mili), record banati hai, `keys.set(key, entry)` karti hai -- aur yeh sab ek hi tick mein. Doosri call jab chalegi, use key mil jaayegi, fingerprint same hai, toh wahi `entry` return.

Entry mein `done` promise hai -- original ke sends ka promise. Isliye 20 ki 20 calls `await entry.done` karti hain aur sab ko FINAL record milta hai (push `sent`), sirf "accepted" nahi. Test "20 concurrent identical requests while the provider is slow" yeh exactly karta hai: ek `gate()` se fake push provider ko hold kiya, 20 `notify()` calls ek saath, phir gate resolve -- `push.attempts` length 1, ek hi record id, aur har result mein delivery `sent`.

Agar koi `await` key check se pehle hota -- jaise `await users.get(userId)` -- toh 20 calls sab await par ruk jaatin, phir sab ek ek karke key check karteen jab koi bhi register nahi hua hota: 20 records, 20 OTPs. Mutation N19 (key not registered) isi test se pakdi gayi.

Honest caveat: yeh guarantee EK process ke andar hai. Do servers ho toh har ek ka apna Map hai; wahan shared store mein atomic "insert if absent" chahiye (DB unique constraint, Redis `SET NX`). Stage 2 mein bhi keys in-memory LRU hain, distributed nahi.
why_needed: Mobile apps aur load balancers requests retry karte hain, aksar parallel. Bina dedupe ke user ko 2-3 OTP milte hain, aur SMS ka bill bhi double.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter par token machine: pehla aadmi token le leta hai, baaki 19 jo usi kaam ke liye aaye the unhe wahi token number bata diya jaata hai aur sab usi ek window ke result ka wait karte hain.
how_it_works: `accept` (sync) -> `keys.get` miss -> `buildRecord` -> `keys.set(key, { fingerprint, recordId, done })` -> `done = run(...)`. Duplicate: `keys.get` hit -> same entry -> `await entry.done` -> `get(recordId)` copy.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::accept` aur `KeyEntry` interface (`fingerprint`, `recordId`, `done: Promise<void>`). `test/idempotency.test.ts` (7 tests) mein yeh test aur "a conflicting request while the original is still sending is refused too". `test/helpers.ts::gate` ek promise hai jo bahar se resolve hota hai -- provider ko "in flight" pakad ke rakhne ke liye. Randomized test mein 15% requests purani key ka retry hain, aur end mein `records.length === keys.length`.
advantages: Koi lock nahi: event loop ki guarantee
Duplicates ko final result milta hai
Test slow provider ke saath, real race
disadvantages: Sirf ek process ke andar valid
Stage 1 mein keys kabhi expire nahi hoti (memory badhti hai)
common_mistakes: Key check se pehle await
Duplicate ko turant 'accepted' return karna bina final result
Process-local Map ko multi-server mein idempotent samajhna
follow_up_questions: How would you make this work across several servers?
What does a duplicate get if the original is still sending?
Why does the test hold the provider with a gate?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Event loop par bharosa karke lock-free aur simple. Keemat: guarantee process boundary par khatam. Duplicate ko original ka promise dene se sab ko same answer milta hai, par duplicate caller original jitna wait karta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Process crash: in-memory key gayi, retry naya record banata hai (at-least-once). Do instances: dono ke Map alag, dono bhejte hain. Code refactor mein koi `await` key check se pehle aa gaya toh silently toot jaata hai -- isliye test.
advanced.alternatives: DB unique index on idempotency_key with insert-first; Redis `SET key NX PX`; ya ek single partitioned consumer per user (Kafka key = userId) jahan ordering se dedupe.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multiple servers par shared store chahiye; 100x par key store ka size aur TTL (stage 2 mein 24 h LRU) aur hot-key contention sochna padta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Keys durable store mein TTL ke saath, response bhi store (HTTP replay ke liye), metrics: duplicates per minute, conflicts per minute.

question: What is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, how is the request fingerprint built, and why does a duplicate of a failed notification not resend?
answer_hinglish:
Idempotency key ka contract: "same key = same request". Agar same key ke saath DIFFERENT request aaye -- alag type, alag user ya alag data -- toh yeh caller ka bug hai (key reuse ho gayi). Project Stripe ki tarah `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` throw karta hai, silently "first one wins" nahi karta. "First one wins" mein caller sochta ki naya OTP `222222` gaya, jabki user ke paas `111111` hai -- login fail aur debug karna mushkil.

Same request kaise pehchaanein? `checkRequest` ek fingerprint banata hai: `stableStringify({ typeId, userId, data })`. `stableStringify` object keys ko SORT karke serialize karta hai, recursively. Isliye `{ orderId: "1", user: { name: "A", tier: "gold" } }` aur `{ user: { tier: "gold", name: "A" }, orderId: "1" }` same fingerprint dete hain -- JSON.stringify yahan alag strings deta, aur client library ka key order badalne par false conflict aata. Mutation N2 (key order matters) caught. Arrays ka order matter karta hai -- woh sahi hai, `[1,2]` aur `[2,1]` alag data hain.

Conflict ka check original ke sending ke DAURAAN bhi hota hai (test "a conflicting request while the original is still sending is refused too") aur original untouched rehta hai.

Failed notification ka duplicate: woh same (failed) record return karta hai, dobara nahi bhejta. Reason: key ka kaam "ek request = ek notification" hai, delivery retry karna nahi. Retry delivery layer ki zimmedari hai (stage 2: backoff, queue). Agar key se resend hota, toh har client retry ek extra provider call ban jaata aur `first` mode ke rules toot sakte the.
why_needed: Keys reuse hoti hain bugs se (constant key, counter reset). Conflict detect na karo toh galat message silently chala jaata hai; key order par false conflict ho toh valid retries fail.
real_world_analogy: Railway ticket ka PNR: same PNR se dobara poocho toh wahi ticket dikhega. Koi same PNR par doosre station ka ticket maange toh counter mana kar dega -- "yeh PNR kisi aur journey ka hai".
how_it_works: `stableStringify`: array -> `[` + elements + `]`; object -> keys `sort()`, har `"key":value` join; baaki `JSON.stringify(value) ?? "undefined"`. `accept` mein `existing.fingerprint !== fingerprint` -> conflict.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::stableStringify` aur `checkRequest`. `test/idempotency.test.ts`: "key order inside data does not matter" (email attempts 1), "same key, different request -> IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; the original is untouched" (code, userId aur typeId teeno badal kar), "a duplicate of a FAILED notification does not resend (retrying a failure is stage 2's job, not the key's)" -- teen channels fail, duplicate ke baad bhi total attempts 3. Mutation N1 (conflict not detected) caught. Stage 3 HTTP mein yeh 409 ban jaata hai.

Key order se false conflict nahi
Delivery retry aur request dedupe alag concerns
disadvantages: Poora fingerprint string memory mein (bada data = badi string); hash nahi kiya
Failed notification ko dobara bhejne ke liye NAYI key chahiye

question: Why must a request be invalid for every user if it is invalid for one -- for example a missing variable on a channel this user would skip, or a channel with no sender?
answer_hinglish:
Rule: request valid hai ya nahi, yeh is par depend nahi karna chahiye ki user KAUN hai ya abhi KYA time hai. Isliye `buildRecord` type ke HAR channel ka template render karta hai aur har channel ka sender check karta hai -- chahe yeh user us channel ko skip kare (no address, muted, deferred).

Socho agar sirf planned channels render hote. `order_shipped` ka email template `{{onlyEmail}}` maangta hai jo caller nahi bhejta. Test mein jo user hai uska email hi nahi -- toh email skip, render nahi, request "pass". Staging mein sab users bina email ke the, sab green. Production mein pehla user jiske paas email hai -- crash ya missing message. Bug user-dependent aur time-dependent ho jaata (raat ko marketing push deferred, din mein render -- din mein hi fail). Aisa bug reproduce karna bahut mushkil hai.

Same logic `NO_SENDER` par: type mein `sms` hai par notifier ko SMS sender nahi diya -- yeh deployment / config ki galti hai. Agar sirf us user ke liye pakdi jaati jiske paas phone hai, toh galti der se dikhti. Test "a type channel without a sender -> NO_SENDER, even if this user has no address for it".

Failure scenario ka doosra hissa: error par koi state nahi badalta (check then change), key free rehti hai, caller theek karke same key se retry karta hai. Stage 3 HTTP mein `NO_SENDER` 500 (server ki galti, message hidden aur logged) aur missing variable 422 hai.

Trade-off: thoda extra rendering kaam har request par. Notification jaise low-CPU kaam mein yeh negligible hai; deterministic validation uske layak hai.
why_needed: User-dependent validation bugs ko staging mein chhupa deta hai aur production mein random users par fodta hai. Deterministic validation caller ko pehli request par hi galti dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Exam paper check karte waqt examiner har sawaal check karta hai, sirf woh nahi jo is student ne attempt kiye -- warna galat answer key tab tak pakdi nahi jaati jab tak koi student woh sawaal attempt na kare.
how_it_works: `type.channels.map(channel => { if (!deps.senders.has(channel)) throw NO_SENDER; renderTemplate(...); applyPlan(..., planChannel(...)) })` -- render aur sender check planning se PEHLE aur har channel par.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::buildRecord` comment: "Every channel of the type is rendered and must have a sender, even one this user will skip: whether a request is valid must not depend on who the user is or what time it is." Tests in `test/notifier.test.ts`: "a variable missing only from a channel the user would skip is still an error (validity does not depend on the user)" aur NO_SENDER wala. Mutation N6 caught. `src/notifier.ts` constructor mein `sendersByChannel` do senders ek channel par refuse karta hai ("two senders for one channel are refused").
advantages: Bugs pehli request par dikhte hain, user par depend nahi
Config galti (missing sender) jaldi pakdi jaati hai
Error par state clean
disadvantages: Har request par skip hone wale channels bhi render (extra CPU)
Ek channel ke template mein galti poore type ko rokti hai
common_mistakes: Sirf planned channels render karna
Sender ko lazily send time par dhoondhna
Missing sender ko 4xx batana (caller ki galti nahi hai)
follow_up_questions: Should NO_SENDER be caught at startup instead of per request?
What is the cost of rendering skipped channels?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Determinism vs thoda extra kaam: har channel render karna CPU leta hai, par validation ka result user / time se independent ho jaata hai. Ek strict rule hai: koi channel broken hai toh type hi unusable -- graceful degradation nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Catalog mein ek channel ke template mein naya variable add hua aur callers update nahi hue -- us type ki SAARI requests fail hongi (achha, loud). Missing sender deploy ke baad pehli request par hi `NO_SENDER` (500) deta hai.
advanced.alternatives: NO_SENDER ko notifier constructor mein catalog ke saath cross-check kar sakte (startup par fail) -- yahan per request hai kyunki catalog baad mein bhi register ho sakta hai. Template variables ka schema per type (JSON schema) se caller-side validation.

question: What does "one runner per record" mean, and how do two concurrent flushDue() calls avoid sending a deferred delivery twice?
answer_hinglish:
"One runner per record" ka matlab: kisi bhi waqt ek record ki deliveries sirf ek `run()` bhej raha ho. `Notifier` ke paas ek `running: Set<string>` hai -- `run()` shuru hote hi record id add hoti hai aur `finally` mein hat-ti hai. `flushDue()` har record par pehle check karta hai `if (this.running.has(record.id)) continue`.

Yeh kyun zaroori hai? Do cases. Pehla: `first` mode record jiska email abhi bhi bhej raha hai (slow provider) aur push deferred tha jo ab due ho gaya. Agar flush push bhi bhej de, toh email aur push dono succeed kar sakte hain -- `first` ne do channels bheje, rule toota. Test "flushDue skips a record whose sends are still running, and picks it up next time" yahi hai; mutation N4 (busy record flushed) caught.

Doosra: do `flushDue()` ek saath (do `setInterval` overlap, ya do callers). Pehla flush synchronous loop mein delivery ko replan karke `pending` banata hai aur `this.run(...)` bulata hai -- `run` async hai, par uski pehli line `running.add` synchronous chalti hai, pehle await se pehle. Doosra flush jab loop chalata hai, record `running` mein hai AUR delivery ab `deferred` nahi rahi, toh skip. Test "two concurrent flushDue calls send a deferred delivery once": results `[1, 0]`, push attempts 1.

Phir se, yeh event-loop guarantee hai, ek process ke liye. Stage 2 mein yahi problem queue leases se solve hoti hai -- kai workers, kai processes, aur har write se pehle lease token check. Stage 1 ka set ek "in-process lock" hai.
why_needed: Overlapping flushes aur slow providers real hain. Bina guard ke ek delivery do baar ja sakti hai ya first mode do channels bhej sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek file par "in use by Ramesh" ka tag: jab tak tag laga hai, doosra clerk us file ko nahi uthaata, chahe uska koi kaam due ho -- next round mein dekhega.
how_it_works: `run(record, selected)`: `this.running.add(record.id)`; try { send } finally { `this.running.delete(record.id)` }. `flushDue`: `if (this.running.has(record.id) || !record.deliveries.some(due)) continue;` -> replan -> `run`.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::flushDue` aur `src/notifier.ts::run`, field `running = new Set<string>() // record ids with sends in progress`. Tests in `test/notifier.test.ts` describe "preferences in the notifier": dono tests `gate()` se provider ko hold karte hain. Randomized test har provider call par check karta hai "first mode: a send after a success" -- ek bhi violation nahi.
advantages: Simple set, koi lock library nahi
first mode ka 'max ek channel' preserve
Busy record next flush mein pick hota hai, khota nahi
disadvantages: Sirf ek process
Busy record ki due delivery ek flush interval late ho sakti hai
common_mistakes: Async function mein running.add ko await ke baad rakhna
finally ke bina delete (throw par record hamesha busy)
Busy record ko skip karne ki jagah wait karna (flush block)
follow_up_questions: How does stage 2 replace this set with leases?
What happens if run() throws?
Why skip instead of waiting for the busy record?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Skip (non-blocking) vs wait: skip se flush kabhi slow provider par atakta nahi, par us record ki due delivery agle flush tak late. In-process set vs distributed lock: set free hai par ek process tak.
advanced.failure_scenarios: `run` ke andar unexpected throw -- `finally` running clear karta hai, warna record forever busy. Process crash: running set gaya, deliveries `sending` state mein atki (stage 1 recover nahi karta; stage 2 leases se karta hai).
advanced.alternatives: Per-record mutex / promise chain; distributed lock (Redis SET NX with TTL); ya queue with visibility timeout jahan ek job ek hi worker ke paas hota hai (stage 2).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Kai processes par yeh set kaam nahi karta -- leases ya partition-by-record chahiye. `flushDue` har record scan karta hai (O(n)); 100x par yeh khud bottleneck.
advanced.production_improvements: Queue-based delivery (stage 2), stuck `sending` deliveries ka recovery, aur metric: kitne records flush mein busy ki wajah se skip hue.

question: Users report a marketing push arriving at 23:00 local even though their quiet hours are 22:00-07:00. The push was deferred correctly the night before. How do you investigate, and what was the bug?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh real bug tha, randomized test ne pakda.

Symptom: delivery raat ko sahi `deferred` hui thi (`notBefore` = subah 07:00), phir bhi agli RAAT 23:00 par push gaya. Investigate kaise: (1) delivery record dekho -- `notBefore` sahi hai, toh planning time ka rule theek tha. (2) Provider call ka time dekho -- 23:00 agle din. Matlab send 16 ghante late hua. (3) `flushDue` kab chala? Woh late chala -- poller ruka tha / process busy tha / interval bada tha. (4) `flushDue` kya check karta tha? Sirf `notBefore <= now`. Bas -- isne yeh nahi socha ki "due" hone aur "ab bhejna theek hai" alag cheezein hain.

Cause: pehla version jo bhi due tha woh bhej deta tha. Jab flush late hua aur agli raat ke quiet hours mein pada, push chala gaya. Aur doosra effect same root cause se (README mein likha hai): user ne deferral ke baad channel mute kiya, phir bhi message gaya. Isi family mein address ka case bhi hai -- planning ke waqt ka address use hota toh badla hua address miss hota (mutation N16 yahi check karti hai).

Fix: due delivery ko send time par DOBARA PLAN karo -- same `planChannel`, user ki CURRENT preferences, CURRENT address aur CURRENT time ke saath (`replan` + `applyPlan`). Result: sent, dobara deferred (naya `notBefore`), ya skipped (`opted_out` / `no_address`).

Regression tests: "a late flush that lands in the NEXT night's quiet hours defers again instead of sending" (agli raat 23:00 par flush 0 bhejta hai, `notBefore` ab 25 tareekh 07:00), "muted after it was deferred -> skipped (opted_out)", "address changed meanwhile -> sent to the CURRENT address". Mutations N5 (no planning again at flush) aur N16 (old address used) caught. Lesson: plan aur send ka time alag ho, toh send ke time dobara decide karo.
why_needed: Deferred / delayed kaam hamesha late chal sakta hai. Jo rule plan ke waqt lagaya woh send ke waqt bhi sach hai, yeh maan lena time-of-check vs time-of-use bug hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ne kal subah ke liye dawai likhi. Tum agle hafte lene gaye toh chemist ko purana parcha nahi, aaj ki halat dekhni chahiye -- shayad ab allergy pata chali hai.
how_it_works: `flushDue`: due deliveries ke liye `applyPlan(delivery, replan(this.deps, record, delivery, now))`; sirf jo `pending` bane unhe `ready` set mein daal kar `run(record, d => ready.has(d))`. `replan` user aur preferences fresh padhta hai.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::flushDue` ka comment bug ki kahani batata hai: "A due delivery is PLANNED AGAIN before it is sent ... (Found by the randomized test: a late flush sent a marketing push inside the user's quiet hours.)" `src/planner.ts::replan`. `test/invariants.test.ts` har provider call par `inQuiet(s.clock.now(), ...)` independently check karta hai -- isi se pakda. Stage 2 ne yahi lesson liya: deferred job jab run hota hai, channel dobara plan hota hai (mutation S5).
advantages: Rule send time par bhi sach
Current address aur preferences use hote hain
Same function, koi duplicate logic nahi
disadvantages: Ek deferred message kai baar defer ho sakta hai (late flushes)
Message ki expiry nahi, toh bahut purana promo bhi jaa sakta hai
common_mistakes: Sirf `notBefore <= now` dekh kar bhejna
Plan ke waqt ka address store karke use karna
Bug ko 'flush interval chhota karo' se patch karna
follow_up_questions: Why is making the flush more frequent not a real fix?
How does stage 2 apply the same lesson to delayed jobs?
Which mutation proves the fix is tested?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Replan har send par ek extra user / preferences lookup karta hai -- sasta, aur correctness ke liye zaroori. Alternative "flush ko kabhi late mat hone do" impossible guarantee hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Poller ruk gaya (deploy, GC pause, process down) -- fix ke saath messages late jaate hain par rules nahi tootte. User delete ho gaya -> `skipped no_address`. Short gap wali window (00:15-00:00) mein hourly flush gap miss karke message ek din aur wait karta hai (randomized seed 5 ne dikhaya).
advanced.alternatives: Deferral ko delayed job banana (stage 2) -- phir bhi job run hone par replan zaroori hai. Message par `expiresAt` lagana taaki bahut late ho toh drop.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Lakhon deferred deliveries par har flush O(n) scan hai; replan per delivery ek lookup. Queue / index on `notBefore` se sirf due wale uthao.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-type expiry, metric "deferred again at flush" aur "sent N hours after notBefore", aur ek alert jab flush lag badhe.

question: What happens in stage 1 when a provider says no, throws an exception, or returns garbage?
answer_hinglish:
`ChannelSender.send()` ka contract hai `sent | failed(retryable, reason)` return karna. Provider ka "no" (galat number, expired token) THROW nahi, `failed` return hona chahiye. Par real code mein SDK throw bhi karte hain aur kabhi ajeeb object bhi return kar dete hain -- notifier ko dono se crash nahi hona chahiye.

Isliye har call `sendOnce` se hoti hai. Sender throw kare -> `failed, retryable: true, reason: "sender threw: ..."`. Retryable kyun? Kyunki outcome UNKNOWN hai -- ho sakta hai provider ne message bhej diya ho aur response aate waqt network toot gaya. Sender garbage return kare (jaise `{ ok: true }`) -> `isSendResult` check fail -> `failed, retryable: true, reason: "sender returned an invalid result"`. Mutations N7 (sender throw not caught) aur N8 (garbage result trusted) caught.

Phir mode decide karta hai: `first` mein permanent, retryable ya throw -- teeno next channel par fall through (OTP push fail -> SMS). `all` mein ek channel ka fail baaki ko nahi rokta. Stage 1 mein retries NAHI hain -- retryable failure bhi final hai (record mein `retryable: true` likha rehta hai taaki pata chale). Retries, backoff aur circuit breaker stage 2 mein aate hain.

Record ka overall status `notificationStatus` se: koi sent -> `delivered`; sab failed -> `failed`; sab skipped -> `suppressed`; kuch deferred -> `scheduled`.
why_needed: Providers fail hote hain, aur unke SDK bhi buggy hote hain. Ek throw se poora notify crash ho toh baaki channels bhi nahi jaate.
real_world_analogy: Courier boy ne bola "address nahi mila" (failed), ya woh bina bataye gayab ho gaya (throw -- pata nahi parcel pahuncha ya nahi). Dono case mein manager crash nahi karta -- next option try karta hai.
how_it_works: `sendOnce(sender, message)`: `try { answer = await sender.send(...); return isSendResult(answer) ? answer : failed-invalid } catch (e) { return failed-threw }`. `recordResult` delivery ka status, error, retryable likhta hai.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::sendOnce`, `isSendResult`, `recordResult`; `src/senders.ts::FakeSender` script se `"throw"` ya koi bhi `SendResult` de sakta hai. Tests: '"first" falls through failures, permanent or retryable, and a throwing sender', '"first": every channel failing -> failed, each tried once in order', "a sender returning garbage is a retryable failure, not a crash", "deferred delivery failing at flush stays failed (stage 1 has no retries)". README demo: push "token expired" fail, SMS sent, email not_needed.

Unknown outcome ko honestly retryable maana

question: Which design pattern does the channel layer use, and why were Singleton, a class per notification type and the State pattern deliberately not used?
answer_hinglish:
Channels Strategy pattern hain. `ChannelSender` ek interface hai -- `channel` aur `send(message, signal?)`. Notifier sirf yeh interface jaanta hai; peeche SES hai, Twilio hai, FCM hai ya `FakeSender`, use farak nahi padta. Naya provider = ek class jo interface implement kare. Tests isi wajah se deterministic hain: `FakeSender` ek script se jawab deta hai (`willAnswer`). Stage 3 ka `InboxSender` bhi bas ek aur strategy hai -- inbox "provider" message store karta hai.

Jo patterns NAHI use kiye, aur kyun -- interview mein yeh bolna senior signal hai:

Singleton notifier nahi: tests har case ke liye naya notifier banate hain (alag clock, alag fakes). Singleton global state hota, tests ek doosre ko affect karte. Ek instance chahiye toh app ke composition root mein ek baar banao -- yeh wiring ka decision hai, class ka nahi.

Class per notification type nahi: `OtpNotification`, `OrderShippedNotification` mein behaviour same hai, sirf data alag. Type data hai -- catalog mein ek object. 50 types = 50 objects, 50 classes nahi.

State pattern nahi: delivery ke statuses (`pending`, `sending`, `sent`, `failed`, `skipped`, `deferred`) ek string field hain jinhe kuch functions guarded tareeke se badalte hain (`applyPlan`, `recordResult`, `markRestNotNeeded`). Har state ki class banane se transitions 6 files mein bikhar jaate, jabki yahan har state ka behaviour alag nahi -- sab ek planner aur ek send path se guzarte hain.

Rule of thumb: pattern tab lagao jab woh variation ko alag kare. Senders mein real variation hai; types aur states mein nahi.
why_needed: Interviewer aksar check karta hai ki candidate patterns ratta maar ke lagata hai ya zaroorat dekh kar. Kya nahi use kiya aur kyun -- yeh design maturity dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein bijli ka socket (Strategy): koi bhi appliance lagao, plug same. Par har bulb ke liye alag switchboard banana (class per type) ya har switch position ka alag electrician (State pattern) -- overkill.
how_it_works: `sendersByChannel(senders)` ek `Map<Channel, ChannelSender>` banata hai (ek channel par do senders error). Delivery bhejte waqt `this.deps.senders.get(delivery.channel)` aur `sendOnce(sender, message)`.
in_this_project: `src/senders.ts` ka header comment: "Channels are a Strategy: the notifier knows ChannelSender, not SES / Twilio / FCM." README "Design choices": "Not used on purpose: a Singleton notifier, a class per type, the State pattern for a delivery (a status field with guarded changes is enough)." `src/types.ts::DeliveryStatus` union. `test/helpers.ts::setup` har test mein naya Notifier banata hai.

Fakes se deterministic tests
Kam classes, kam indirection
disadvantages: Status string par compiler transitions enforce nahi karta (guards functions mein)
Ek channel par ek hi sender (multi-provider failover nahi)

Har notification type ki subclass
Har delivery state ki class

Data-driven types flexible hain par type-specific custom logic (jaise "weekly digest data khud fetch kare") ke liye hook nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek sender interface tod de (throw on 'no') -- `sendOnce` bachaata hai. Do senders ek channel par -- constructor refuse karta hai. Status field ko koi galat jagah se set kare -- koi type-level guard nahi.

question: How does the stage 1 randomized invariant test work, why does it re-compute the rules independently, and what did it find?
answer_hinglish:
Unit tests woh cases check karte hain jo humne socha. Randomized test woh dhoondhta hai jo nahi socha. `test/invariants.test.ts` mein 8 seeds hain, har seed 300 requests. Ek seeded PRNG se: 12 users random offsets ke saath (`-300, 0, 60, 330, 345, 600`), random addresses (email 80%, phone 60%, push 60%), random mutes, aur 60% users ki random quiet window (15 minute multiples). Har request se pehle clock 0-39 minute aage, 15% requests purani key ka retry, random `flushDue`. Providers 15% fail (retryable ya permanent), 5% throw.

Sabse important design: rules ko test mein INDEPENDENTLY re-compute kiya, `policy.ts` se nahi. `inQuiet` `Date` ke `getUTCHours` / `getUTCMinutes` use karta hai, modulo arithmetic nahi. Agar test bhi `quietUntil` bulata toh dono mein same bug hota aur test green rehta. Aur check HAR provider call ke MOMENT par hota hai: galat address, muted marketing channel bheja, SMS / push quiet hours mein, `first` mode mein success ke baad ek aur send.

End par: 2 din tak har 15 minute flush, phir assert -- violations khaali, ek record per key, har record finished, attempts <= 1, `no_address` aur `opted_out` reasons exactly sahi, aur provider calls = records mein likhe attempts.

Kya mila: (1) late-flush bug -- flush late chala aur agli raat ke quiet hours mein push bheja; fix: send time par replan. (2) Hourly flushes ek chhota gap (23h45m window ka 15 minute gap) hamesha miss kar sakte hain -- seed 5 ne dikhaya. Yeh limitation README mein documented hai, aur test 15 minute flush use karta hai.
why_needed: Time, preferences aur concurrency ke combinations itne zyada hain ki hand-written cases kam padte hain. Invariants + random inputs un combinations ko explore karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek naye driver ko sirf fixed route par test karne ki jagah random sheher, random time aur random traffic mein chalwana, aur har mod par ek alag examiner apni ghadi se rule check kare -- driver ki ghadi se nahi.
how_it_works: `prng(seed)` (mulberry32-style) deterministic randomness deta hai -- fail hua toh same seed se reproduce. Fake senders `willAnswer(...2000 x outcome)` se har call par `outcome(m)` chalate hain jo rule check karke random jawab deta hai.
in_this_project: `test/invariants.test.ts`: `inQuiet`, `ADDRESS`, `TYPES = ["otp", "order_shipped", "sale", "promo_first"]`, comment "Flushes every 15 minutes for two days ... (hourly flushes can miss such a gap forever -- seed 5 did)". README tests table: "8 seeds x 300 requests ... every send is checked at the moment it happens against rules re-computed independently (Date arithmetic, not policy.ts)". Stage 2 ne isi idea ko `test/queued-invariants.test.ts` mein dying workers ke saath badhaya.

Independent oracle: same bug dono jagah nahi
Seeded: fail reproducible
disadvantages: 8 seeds limited hain; coverage ki guarantee nahi
Oracle khud galat ho sakta hai
Fake time; real timers ke bugs nahi pakdta

Sirf end state check karna, send ke moment par nahi

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Randomized test example tests ki jagah nahi, unke upar hai: examples boundaries lock karte hain, random test combinations explore karta hai. Independent oracle likhne mein extra code hai, par wahi test ko meaningful banata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Oracle aur code dono ek hi galat assumption share karein (jaise dono DST ignore karte hain) toh test kuch nahi pakdega -- yeh DST ke liye sach hai. Flaky nahi hai kyunki seeded aur ManualClock.
advanced.alternatives: fast-check jaisi property-based library (automatic shrinking ke saath minimal failing case), model-based testing (ek simple reference model ke saath compare), ya mutation testing (yahan 43 checks se suite ki taakat naapi).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Seeds aur requests badhao toh runtime badhta hai; CI mein kuch seeds, nightly mein hazaaron. Stage 2 mein workers aur leases ke saath state space bahut bada ho jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Shrinking add karna, failing seed ko permanent regression case banana, aur production mein bhi same invariant ek monitor ki tarah: "marketing sends in user's quiet hours" ka count 0 hona chahiye.

question: Exercise: some regions require opt-in for marketing SMS. Add this as a change to planChannel and the preferences, with tests.
answer_hinglish:
README ke "Known and NOT handled" mein likha hai: marketing default allowed hai (opt-out model); kuch jurisdictions marketing SMS / email ke liye opt-in maangte hain; "that is a policy change in one function, not built". Yeh exercise wahi change hai -- aur yeh dikhata hai ki rule ek jagah hone ka faayda kya hai.

Plan: (1) `Preferences` mein ek optional field `optedInMarketing?: Channel[]` -- jin channels par user ne explicitly haan bola. (2) Ek constant `OPT_IN_REQUIRED: ReadonlySet<Channel>` (ya config), jaise `new Set(["sms"])`. (3) `planChannel` mein mute check ke saath: marketing hai, channel opt-in maangta hai, aur user ne opt in nahi kiya -> `skipped (opted_out)`. Naya skip reason bhi bana sakte ho (`no_consent`) -- woh reporting ke liye better hai, par `SkipReason` union aur HTTP output dono badalte hain; yahan simple rakha. (4) `PreferenceStore.set` naye field ko validate kare (list of known channels) aur `get` copy kare -- warna stage 3 ka null-bug jaisa phir hoga.

Transactional par koi asar nahi -- woh check se pehle return ho jaata hai. Quiet hours ka order: consent check quiet hours se PEHLE, taaki bina consent wala message defer na ho (defer = baad mein bhejenge, jo galat hai).

Aur `replan` free mein sahi ho jaata hai: deferred SMS jiska user ne baad mein opt-in hataya, flush par skip hoga -- kyunki send time par wahi function chalta hai. Solution illustrative hai, repo mein built nahi.

real_world_analogy: Society mein naya rule: "salesman sirf unke ghar jaayega jinhone register mein naam likha hai". Guard ke rulebook mein ek line add hoti hai -- har ghar ka darwaza nahi badalta.
