question: Exercise: this toy notifier sends a duplicate OTP when the client retries concurrently. Find the bug, fix it, and write the test that proves it.
answer_hinglish:
Buggy code mein key check se PEHLE ek `await` hai (`await this.users.get(...)`, jaise ek async user service). 20 concurrent calls sab pehle await par ruk jaati hain; phir har ek resume hoti hai aur `keys.has(key)` check karti hai -- par ab tak kisi ne `keys.set` nahi kiya (woh send ke BAAD hai). Toh sab 20 aage badhti hain: 20 sends. Yeh classic check-then-act race hai, JavaScript single-threaded hone ke bawajood -- kyunki `await` ek yield point hai.

Fix ke do hisse. Pehla: key ko CLAIM karo synchronous step mein, kisi bhi await se pehle, aur claim ke saath ek promise store karo jo final result dega. Duplicate us promise ko await karta hai -- usse wahi record milta hai, naya send nahi. Doosra: agar validation async hi hai (user lookup), toh failure par claim hatao, taaki "error = nothing happened" aur key free rahe. Project ka `Notifier` isse simpler hai: wahan saari lookups synchronous hain, isliye key register karne se pehle sab validation ho jaata hai aur kuch hatana nahi padta.

Fingerprint bhi store karo, warna same key ke saath alag request ko silently purana result milta hai.

Test: provider ko ek `gate()` se hold karo taaki race window khuli rahe, 20 calls ek saath bhejo, phir gate kholo, aur assert karo: provider attempts 1, sab results ki id same. Bina gate ke test kabhi kabhi pass ho jaata (race ko mauka hi nahi milta) -- yeh test ko meaningful banata hai. Solution illustrative hai; asli version `src/notifier.ts::accept` aur `test/idempotency.test.ts` mein hai.
why_needed: "Node single-threaded hai toh race nahi hogi" ek common galatfehmi hai. Har await par doosra kaam chal sakta hai; idempotency ko yeh samajh kar likhna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Do log ek hi movie ticket ke liye counter par: dono ne poocha "seat khaali hai?" -- haan; dono payment karne chale gaye; dono ko same seat mili. Sahi tareeka: poochte hi seat ko "on hold" mark karo.
how_it_works: Claim-first: `keys.set(key, { fingerprint, done })` synchronous; `done` = async work ka promise; duplicate -> `await existing.done`; async validation fail -> `keys.delete(key)` aur rethrow.
in_this_project: Asli implementation: `src/notifier.ts::accept` ("synchronous: throws before anything is stored") aur `KeyEntry.done`. Test: `test/idempotency.test.ts` "20 concurrent identical requests while the provider is slow". `test/helpers.ts::gate`. Mutation N19 (key not registered) isi test se caught. Stage 3 HTTP layer `getByKey` aur `notify()` ke beech koi await nahi rakhta, isi wajah se.
advantages: Claim-first pattern lock ke bina race band karta hai
Duplicates ko same final result
Gate se race deterministic test
disadvantages: Async validation ke saath claim release ka extra code
Process-local; multi-server par shared store chahiye
common_mistakes: Key ko send ke baad set karna
Failure par claim na hatana (key hamesha 'used')
Bina gate ke concurrency test likhna
follow_up_questions: How does the claim-first idea map to a database unique constraint?
What if a duplicate arrives after the original failed validation?
Why does the HTTP layer keep getByKey and notify() back to back?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Claim-first vs lock: claim-first koi waiting queue nahi banata, sab ek promise share karte hain. Failure par release karna padta hai, warna key leak. Project ka notifier sab validation synchronous rakh kar release ki zaroorat hi khatam karta hai -- simpler, par user directory async service ho toh yeh pattern chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Original crash ho jaaye promise ke beech -- in-memory mein sab chala gaya. Release ka race: naya claim aa chuka ho aur purana catch use delete kar de -- isliye `done === done` check. Bahut lamba original: duplicates utni der wait karte hain.
advanced.alternatives: DB: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (insert-first, phir kaam), Redis `SET NX PX`, ya per-key single-flight (cache-kit ka `getOrLoad` jaisa).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-instance par process Map bekaar; shared store chahiye, aur keys ka TTL (stage 2: 24 h LRU). Hot key (ek user ka retry storm) ek promise par sab ko attach karta hai -- sasta.
advanced.production_improvements: Shared durable key store, stored response for replays, conflict metrics, aur ek lint / review rule: idempotency check se pehle koi await nahi.

question: Stage 1 keeps everything in memory. How would you model the catalog, preferences, notification records and idempotency keys in a relational database?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honestly: is project mein koi database nahi hai. Records, keys, preferences aur catalog sab Maps hain; restart par sab gaya (README "Everything is in memory"). Par code ki shapes seedha tables ban sakti hain, aur interview mein main yeh design bataunga.

`notification_types`: id (PK), category, mode, channels (ordered array / JSON), aur `notification_templates` (type_id, channel, subject, body; PK type_id + channel). Validation wahi rahegi jo `register()` karta hai -- app mein, likhte waqt.

`user_preferences`: user_id (PK), muted_marketing (array), quiet_start, quiet_end, aur user ka zone (offset nahi -- DST). Whole replacement (PUT) se ek row update.

`notifications`: id (PK), idempotency_key UNIQUE, fingerprint, type_id, user_id, category, mode, created_at. `deliveries`: (notification_id, channel) PK, status, to_address, subject, body, attempts, not_before, skip_reason, provider_id, error, retryable. Index `(status, not_before)` WHERE status = 'deferred' -- taaki `flushDue` poora table scan na kare, sirf due rows uthaaye (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` se kai workers).

Idempotency ka atomic version: in-memory synchronous trick DB par nahi chalti. Wahan `INSERT INTO notifications ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id` -- jo insert jeeta wahi bhejega; haara hua existing row padhkar fingerprint compare karta hai (alag -> conflict). Notification aur uski deliveries ek transaction mein -- "check everything, then change state" ka DB roop. Keys ka TTL: `created_at` par cleanup job (stage 2 in-memory mein 24 h).

Body rendered store karna (template nahi) zaroori hai: template baad mein badle toh deferred message wahi jaana chahiye jo plan hua tha.
why_needed: Real system mein restart, kai instances aur audit ke liye durable store chahiye. Schema mein woh guarantees aani chahiye jo abhi event loop deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek register jisme har parcel ki ek line hai (notifications) aur har delivery attempt ki ek sub-line (deliveries); tracking number unique hai, toh same parcel do baar enter hi nahi ho sakta.
how_it_works: Unique constraint idempotency deta hai; transaction validate-then-commit deta hai; partial index deferred lookup ko sasta karta hai; SKIP LOCKED concurrent flushers ko ek row par takraane se bachata hai.
in_this_project: Shapes code mein: `src/record.ts` (`NotificationRecord`, `Delivery`), `src/catalog.ts::NotificationTypeDef`, `src/preferences.ts::Preferences`. Stage 1 `Notifier` mein `records` aur `keys` Maps hain; keys kabhi expire nahi hoti (README Known). Stage 2 README kehta hai queue ka interface Postgres table claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` jaisa hai, par built nahi.
code_example:
-- illustrative schema (NOT in this repo; Postgres)
CREATE TABLE notifications (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  fingerprint     text NOT NULL,
  type_id         text NOT NULL REFERENCES notification_types(id),
  user_id         text NOT NULL,
  category        text NOT NULL,
  mode            text NOT NULL,
  created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE deliveries (
  notification_id uuid REFERENCES notifications(id),
  channel         text NOT NULL,
  status          text NOT NULL,
  to_address      text,
  subject         text,
  body            text NOT NULL,       -- rendered at notify time
  attempts        int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  not_before      timestamptz,
  skip_reason     text,
  provider_id     text,
  error           text,
  PRIMARY KEY (notification_id, channel)
);
CREATE INDEX deliveries_due ON deliveries (not_before) WHERE status = 'deferred';

-- idempotent insert: the winner sends, the loser reads the row and compares fingerprints
INSERT INTO notifications (id, idempotency_key, fingerprint, type_id, user_id, category, mode)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7)
ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id;
advantages: Unique constraint cross-instance idempotency deta hai
Partial index se due lookup sasta
Rendered body: template change se plan nahi badalta
disadvantages: Har notify ek write transaction
Records ki retention / partitioning sochni padti hai
Body store karna = PII storage
common_mistakes: Idempotency app memory mein rakhna multi-instance par
Template store karke send time par render (beech mein template badla)
deferred rows ke liye index na banana
follow_up_questions: How would you partition deliveries at a billion rows?
Where does the fingerprint compare happen in the SQL version?
How long do you keep idempotency keys and records?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Relational DB strong consistency aur unique constraints deta hai; write throughput limit hai. Key-value store (DynamoDB conditional put) scale karta hai par joins / reporting kam. Records aur keys ek table mein rakhna simple hai, par key TTL aur record retention alag ho toh do tables better.
advanced.failure_scenarios: DB down: notify fail hona chahiye (error = nothing happened), half write nahi. Insert jeeta par process send se pehle mar gaya -- delivery `pending` padi; ek sweeper / queue chahiye (stage 2 ka kaam). Clock skew: `not_before` DB time se compare karo, app time se nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Outbox pattern: notification row aur ek outbox event ek transaction mein, worker outbox padhe. Event-sourced deliveries (har status change ek row) audit ke liye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: indexes aur connection pool. 100x: user_id ya created_at se partition, purane partitions drop (retention), deliveries ko hot table aur archive mein baantna, key table par TTL cleanup.
advanced.production_improvements: Retention policy (jaise 90 din), PII ke liye body encryption ya sirf template id + data hash, aur metrics: oldest deferred row age, conflict rate.

question: flushDue() is polled and scans every record. What does that cost, how often must it run, and how would you scale deferred delivery?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 1 ka `flushDue()` `this.records.values()` par poora loop chalata hai aur har record ki deliveries mein due wali dhoondhta hai. Matlab cost records ki total ginti ke proportional hai (O(n)), chahe due sirf 2 hon. Aur records kabhi remove nahi hote, toh har flush time ke saath mehenga hota jaata hai. Is project mein koi benchmark nahi hai -- yeh code padh kar complexity ka argument hai, koi measured number nahi.

Polling ka doosra cost latency hai: deferred message tab jaata hai jab agla flush chale. README ke "Known" mein ek subtle case hai: agar quiet window ka gap chhota hai (quiet 00:15-00:00, sirf 15 minute khula), toh flush us gap mein chalna chahiye. Hourly flush gap miss kar sakta hai -- tab replan message ko agle din tak defer kar deta hai, aur yeh har din repeat ho sakta hai. Randomized test ka seed 5 yahi dikhata tha; isliye test 15 minute flush karta hai (windows aur offsets 15 minute multiples hain). Rule of thumb: flush interval sabse chhote allowed gap se chhota ho, ya gaps par minimum lagao.

Scale kaise: (1) deferred deliveries ko `notBefore` se sorted structure mein rakho (min-heap ya DB index) -- sirf due wale uthao, O(due log n). (2) Better: deferral ko delayed job banao -- stage 2 exactly yahi karta hai (`runAt = notBefore`), koi poll scan nahi; job run hone par channel replan hota hai. (3) 07:00 par thundering herd: lakhon deferred ek saath due honge, kyunki bahut users ka window end same hai -- small random jitter add karo ya rate-limit karke spread karo.
why_needed: Deferred delivery ki correctness (replan) solve hai; uski cost aur latency poll design par depend karti hai. Interview mein yeh scale wala follow-up hamesha aata hai.
real_world_analogy: Postman jo har ghante poora mohalla ghoomta hai yeh dekhne ki kisi ka parcel ab dene layak hua ya nahi -- vs ek diary jisme time ke order mein likha hai kaunsa parcel kab dena hai, aur woh sirf agla entry dekhta hai.
how_it_works: Abhi: `for (record of records.values()) if (!running.has && some(due)) ...`. Heap / index: `while (heap.peek().notBefore <= now) pop`. Delayed jobs: queue khud runAt ke hisaab se claim karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/notifier.ts::flushDue` (scan), README "Known and NOT handled (stage 1)": "`flushDue()` is polled ... the randomized test showed this with hourly flushes", aur "Everything is in memory". Stage 2 PLAN: "Deferred deliveries are delayed jobs (runAt = notBefore), so there is no flushDue poll". Stage 2 ki queue bhi `claim()` mein har job scan karti hai (O(n)) -- README mein documented, par woh stage 2 ka topic hai.
advantages: Simple, koi extra structure nahi
Replan ke saath late flush bhi correct
Stage 2 path clear
disadvantages: O(n) har flush, n kabhi ghat-ta nahi
Latency = poll interval
Chhote gaps miss ho sakte hain
common_mistakes: Flush interval ko window gaps se bada rakhna
Records kabhi delete na karna
07:00 herd ke liye koi spreading nahi
follow_up_questions: How do you avoid the 07:00 thundering herd?
Why does the stage 2 delayed job still need to replan?
What would you index in a database for due deliveries?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Poll + scan sabse simple hai aur stage 1 ke chhote scale par theek. Heap fast hai par process memory mein (crash par gaya). Delayed jobs durable aur distributed ho sakte hain par queue infrastructure chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Poller ruk gaya -> sab deferred atke, phir ek saath (replan safe rakhta hai). Records badhte gaye -> flush slow, event loop block, baaki requests latency. Chhota gap miss -> message din-ba-din defer.
advanced.alternatives: Min-heap / timer wheel in-process; DB partial index + `SKIP LOCKED`; Redis sorted set (score = notBefore) with `ZRANGEBYSCORE`; queue delayed messages (SQS delay max 15 min, isliye lambe delay ke liye scheduler); stage 2 ka delayed job.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x records: scan noticeable. 100x: scan unusable -- index / sorted set / queue zaroori, aur deferred sends ko time par spread karna padta hai taaki providers rate-limit na karein.
advanced.production_improvements: Delayed jobs with replan (stage 2), retention jo finished records hataaye, jitter on window end, metric: deferred backlog size aur "sent minus notBefore" lag.

question: In an LLD interview, how would you present this stage 1 design component by component, and where does it stop being enough?
answer_hinglish:
Main 5 components se shuru karunga, har ek ki ek zimmedari. (1) `NotificationCatalog` -- types as data, validated at registration, stored copy. (2) Template renderer (`template.ts`) -- `{{a.b}}`, missing value error, own properties, HTML escape sirf email body. (3) `PreferenceStore` + `quietUntil` -- user choices aur time arithmetic. (4) `planChannel` -- THE rule, pure function. (5) `Notifier` -- idempotency, `all` / `first` modes, `flushDue`. Plus do interfaces jo bahar ki duniya ko abstract karte hain: `ChannelSender` (Strategy, providers) aur `UserDirectory` (addresses kahin aur se aate hain), aur ek `Clock` jo time inject karta hai.

Phir request lifecycle ek line mein: validate + render + plan synchronous, store + key register, phir send; deferred baad mein replan ke saath. Phir 3 hard decisions: key before the first await, check-then-change, send time par replan. Aur numbers jo sach hain: stage 1 ke 81 tests, 43 mutation checks sab caught (do survivors Q5 aur C2 pehle test gaps the, band kiye).

Kahan kaafi nahi: (a) sab in memory, ek process -- restart par records, keys, deferred sab gaye. (b) Koi retry nahi -- retryable fail bhi final. (c) `notify()` sends ke liye wait karta hai -- slow provider caller ko slow karta hai. (d) Keys kabhi expire nahi. (e) `flushDue` poll + scan. Stage 2 yahi solve karta hai: `QueuedNotifier` notify par sirf queue karta hai, workers leases ke saath bhejte hain, retries delayed jobs hain, breaker aur timeout per channel, caps, aur keys 24 h LRU mein. Important: stage 2 ne stage 1 ka shared logic `planner.ts` mein nikala aur 81 tests bina badle regression guard rahe.
why_needed: LLD round mein structure aur reasoning dono chahiye. Clear components + honest limits + "next step kya hai" -- yeh senior answer ka format hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek restaurant ka kitchen: menu (catalog), recipe card (templates), customer ki allergy list (preferences), head chef ka rule "kya serve hoga" (planChannel), aur waiter jo order ek hi baar kitchen tak le jaata hai (Notifier). Chhota restaurant aise chalta hai; chain banane ke liye central kitchen aur delivery fleet (stage 2) chahiye.
how_it_works: `Notifier` constructor mein dependencies inject: catalog, users, preferences, senders, clock, newId. Koi global nahi. `planner.ts` ka shared code dono notifiers use karte hain.
in_this_project: `src/index.ts` public exports. `src/notifier.ts` header comment do halves aur one-runner rule describe karta hai. `src/planner.ts` header: "The part of notify() that both notifiers share". README "Design choices" aur "Known and NOT handled (stage 1)". PLAN.md "Why this project" aur stage table (stage 1 DONE 2026-11-23). Final state: 192 tests across stages.

Sab dependencies inject: testable
Limits clear aur stage 2 ka raasta defined
disadvantages: Ek process, in-memory
notify() send ka wait karta hai
Retries aur backpressure nahi
common_mistakes: Interview mein seedha Kafka se shuru karna bina LLD rules ke
Limitations chhupana
Har cheez ko class banana (types, states)

What changes first if traffic grows 100x?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: In-process synchronous design: samajhna, test karna aur interview mein explain karna aasan; par caller provider ki latency jhelta hai aur crash par sab khota hai. Queue-based design (stage 2) durable aur scalable hai par at-least-once ke saath aata hai -- provider idempotency key chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Process crash: deliveries `sending` mein atki, keys gayi, retry naya record. Slow provider: notify() ke callers slow. Memory: records aur keys bina limit badhte hain.
advanced.alternatives: Stage 2 ka QueuedNotifier (queue + workers + leases); managed services (SNS / FCM topics, SES) ke saath ek thin orchestrator; ya ek event-driven pipeline (Kafka, user id se partition).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: async sends aur bounded keys. 100x: queue, horizontally scaled workers, per-channel breakers aur provider rate limits, DB-backed records with retention, sharded by user. Rules (planChannel) waise hi rehte hain -- yahi LLD ka faayda hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Durable store, queue, retries with backoff, per-channel breaker, caps, HTTP API, delivery receipts, multiple devices aur inbox -- yeh sab stage 2 aur 3 mein aaye; DST-aware zones aur real providers abhi bhi nahi.
